steps.path: Every notice
steps.headline: Should notices that mean the same thing use the same sentence?
steps.today: About 30 notices say one of three things in many different wordings. A stop that wasn't confirmed alone has 5 sentences. A few show raw technical text, like "Control incarnation ended before invocation".
steps.problem: Different words for the same thing make you wonder whether they are different problems, and technical text tells you nothing.
steps.proposal: Three shared sentences, each naming what you tried: "Stop didn't go through." / "Can't tell if Stop went through. Check the chat before trying again." / "Stop isn't available here." with the reason after. Technical text is never shown.

options.label: Shared sentences
pros: One wording to learn per situation.
No technical text ever reaches you.
cons: Loses some detail a few notices give today, like "your phone was offline"; that detail can stay as a second sentence.

options.label: Only replace the technical text
pros: Smallest change.
cons: The many wordings stay.

steps.resolved: Shared sentences. A second sentence only when it changes what you do, like "you're offline, reconnect first"; otherwise dropped. Applied to every row in the list below.

steps.headline: Should "for your information" notices that blocked nothing be short floating ones?
steps.today: Two notices were sorted into the strip: "Attachments were left out of that command" and "There's no reply to copy yet."

steps.path: Using the app from a browser on another device
steps.headline: Should "not available from another device yet" be a short notice instead of one you must close?
steps.today: When you use the app from a browser on another device, some screens (like browsing themes) show "Theme browsing isn't available via remote access yet." It was sorted as a notice that stays until you close it.
steps.problem: There is nothing you can do about it, and it can come back each time you open such a screen, adding a Close press every time.
steps.proposal: Make it a short floating notice with a clearer line: "Browsing themes only works on the computer running YouCoded for now." Yes changes it; No keeps it until closed.

steps.path: The "resume a chat" list and the screen for moving a chat between devices
steps.headline: Should notices from those two screens show on the screen itself, not in a chat's strip?
steps.today: Three failures (a chat couldn't be resumed, moving a chat isn't available, finish the current move first) were sorted into the strip. The moving screen also already has its own Try again and Continue buttons.
steps.problem: The strip belongs to the chat you have open, which may have nothing to do with the screen you are on, and the moving screen would show two sets of buttons for one problem.
steps.proposal: Show them on the screen that raised them, using its own buttons. Yes moves them; No keeps them in the strip.

steps.path: Inside a chat, after /compact or /clear fails
steps.headline: What happens to the "Couldn't compact" card in the chat once it works?
steps.today: You chose that a compact or clear failure shows as a card inside the chat with Try again.
steps.problem: If the card stays after Try again succeeds, the chat shows "Couldn't compact" above a chat that was compacted.
steps.proposal: Pick what the card does next.

options.label: Leaves once it works
pros: The chat only shows what is true now.
cons: No record that it failed once.

options.label: Stays, with a "Worked on retry" line added
pros: A full record in the chat.
cons: More clutter in the chat for something already fixed.

steps.path: A failure in a chat you are not looking at
steps.headline: When something fails in a chat you've switched away from, how should you find out?
steps.today: Some failures arrive a moment later. With notices now tied to their chat, one can land in a chat you have just left.
steps.problem: You would not see it until you happen to go back to that chat.
steps.proposal: Pick how that chat tells you.

options.label: A red dot on that chat in the list
pros: You see which chat needs you without leaving the one you're in.
cons: One more kind of dot in the list.

options.label: A short floating notice naming the chat
pros: Hard to miss.
cons: Interrupts the chat you're in for another one.

options.label: Nothing until you go back
pros: Quietest.
cons: Easy to miss a failed stop or clear.

steps.path: Two notices at the same moment
steps.headline: When two "needs you" notices arrive together, should they take turns?
steps.today: There is one floating notice spot. A second notice replaces the first, so a "needs you" notice can vanish without you pressing anything (for example two at startup).
steps.problem: A notice you were supposed to act on disappears unseen.
steps.proposal: They take turns: the next shows when you close the first. Quick ones like "Copied" show right away and never push a "needs you" notice out. Yes does this; No keeps one spot.

steps.path: The strip above the message box, on a phone
steps.headline: On a narrow phone screen, should the strip's buttons sit under the words instead of beside them?
steps.today: The strip puts up to three buttons (Dismiss, Send anyway, Show card) beside the sentence.
steps.problem: On a phone that squeezes the sentence into a thin column of wrapped words, which you disliked on an earlier round.
steps.proposal: On narrow screens, buttons drop to their own row below the sentence. Yes does this; No keeps them beside the words.

steps.headline: What changed while building

calls.call: Held back for a chat you aren't in also shows a short floating notice naming it.
calls.why: So a refused send in the background is never invisible.

calls.call: Only red failures put a dot on a chat; amber "not sure" ones don't.
calls.why: The dot is for failures, as approved.

calls.call: Busy and not-running notices leave on their own when the app sees the change; otherwise on your next action.
calls.why: Some changes the app can't see right away.

calls.call: "Needs you" notices: none dropped, "1 more" shown.
calls.why: Was "up to three, extras dropped"; the design review found that could hide a failure.

calls.call: Repeated Office save failures merge into one notice.
calls.why: Otherwise a stuck file filled the queue.

calls.call: The red card leaves when Try again works or you send; its Details hold the computer's reason.
calls.why: The only place technical text shows.

calls.call: "Not available in a terminal session" stays floating.
calls.why: Terminal sessions have no message box to hold a strip.

calls.call: "Which one?" is a strip question, not a pop-up in the command list.
calls.why: By the time you press Enter the list has closed.

calls.call: Greyed skills are greyed in a chat's command list; the Skills library page is unchanged.
calls.why: Kept to where the skill is started.

calls.call: Unreadable skills are greyed in every kind of chat.
calls.why: Every chat reads the same file.

calls.call: The held-back strip re-checks instantly; once a second only on the phone's own app.
calls.why: Instant needs no timer where the app is told.

calls.call: A chat covered by Settings, the Marketplace or a page counts as not seen.
calls.why: Found in review: a failure then showed nothing.

calls.call: A refused close says "Couldn't close X. Your computer didn't accept the request."
calls.why: The technical reason was removed; the second sentence is new and in the wording pass.

calls.call: A refused download with an unknown reason says only "Couldn't download X."
calls.why: Found by the grader: it showed technical text.

calls.call: The red dot shows in the window where the failure happened.
calls.why: As planned and listed before the build.

calls.call: The red card's Try again: a "still working" notice didn't leave by itself.
calls.why: Fixed.

calls.call: The red card shows the computer's reason under Details.
calls.why: Kept; now written as the one exception.

calls.call: Your question: simplify the message types.
calls.why: Done: the two look-alike notice bars are one piece, three helpers are one, sentences live in one file.

calls.why: Fixed: it now gets the red dot.
